transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jill Carter (Montclair InfoSec), Tom Wu (Procurement), Maria Gomez (CTO)

Auto-generated sections:
Summary: Walkthrough SIG/CAIQ-style questionnaire; flagged a few items for evidence (SOC2, pen test, architecture diagram, KMS details).
Topics: SOC 2 / ISO, RBAC & SSO, audit logs & retention, data residency, encryption (KMS/HSM), evidence delivery process.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, um thanks for carving out time. I'm Alex Lee, I'm the AE on the account, and Priya is our solutions engineer. We wanted to run through the SIG that you sent and call out any places where you'll need evidence or clarifications.
[00:22] Jill (Montclair): Thanks Alex. Yeah we got a pretty comprehensive questionnaire from our vendor risk team. There are quite a few asks around SOC 2, encryption keys, RBAC and, like, how logs are retained. We wanted to make sure we have the right artifacts before we hand it off.
[00:36] Priya (Redwood-SE): Great, thanks Jill. We'll try to be pragmatic - point out what we can share directly and what typically needs a redaction. Quick FYI: we host for most customers on our hosted platform but can support dedicated or private with different controls. For the SIG answers we usually mark which controls apply for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private.
[00:56] Maria (Montclair-CTO): One question up front: for data residency, we need to know whether customer data can be kept in EU only. Is that something Redwood supports?
[01:08] Alex (Redwood): Yes - we have region pinning in our private and dedicated offerings, and for hosted we have specific cloud regions we can route to, though for strict data residency we typically recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll point you to the region options in the answer.
[01:22] Jill: Okay, good. On SOC 2, do you have a Type II report and is the report public or under NDA?
[01:30] Priya: We do have a SOC 2 Type II. We can share the full report under an NDA, and we typically provide an executive summary or attestation letter for initial review. We'll put the SOC2 link in the evidence bundle and note the process to request the full report.
[01:43] Tom (Procurement): And pen test? Our team wants to see the last external penetration test summary, not necessarily the raw vuln reports.
[01:51] Priya: Yep, we can provide the pen test executive summary and remediation status. For raw reports we usually redact customer-identifying info and handle on a case-by-case basis.
[02:05] Alex: For the SIG fields around KMS, we want to be clear: Redwood integrates with customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and supports BYOK patterns; for Hosted we support cloud KMS where keys are managed by Redwood's cloud account, with customer separation at the tenant level - we'll call this out in the answer.
[02:23] Jill: The questionnaire also asks about HSM, like whether keys ever leave an HSM boundary. Can you explain that?
[02:30] Priya: Short answer: in our Private and Dedicated models we can support HSM-backed keys (Cloud HSM or customer HSM). For Hosted, keys are managed by the cloud provider's KMS; they don't export plaintext keys from the HSM. We'll include exact language around key import/export and whether we have KMS rotation windows.
[02:46] Maria: On RBAC and SSO - we use SAML 2.0 SSO and need SCIM provisioning. Does Redwood support SCIM and SAML?
[02:55] Alex: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. For enterprise plans we also offer fine-grained RBAC with admin/editor/viewer roles and token scoping. We'll flag the default role mappings and point to the docs for role overrides.
[03:12] Jill: Do you log admin actions? Our audit requirements want a tamper-evident audit trail for admin changes and API key rotations.
[03:19] Priya: We capture audit logs on changes to RBAC, API key lifecycle events, model deployments, and configuration changes. Logs are stored in an append-only storage with integrity checks - we'll provide the retention window and can export logs for a customer's SIEM. We'll also mention log forwarding options (S3, syslog, or API).
[03:40] Tom: The SIG has a question about encryption in transit and at rest - what ciphers and TLS versions do you support?
[03:48] Priya: We enforce TLS 1.2+ and prefer TLS 1.3 where supported. For at-rest encryption we use AES-256 for blobs. We'll include cipher suites and minimum TLS versions in the evidence.
[04:00] Jill: On data retention - the form asks how long logs and data are kept. What are the defaults?
[04:08] Alex: Default conversational data retention for hosted is 90 days for logs and 365 days for audit logs, but retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private. We'll put the retention matrix in the answer and call out how to request alterations.
[04:22] Maria: Are you able to provide architecture diagrams showing network segmentation and where the model runtime executes?
[04:30] Priya: Yes, we'll share a redacted architecture diagram showing VPC boundaries, subnet segmentation, and where data is decrypted (for BYOK scenarios). We'll also annotate third-party dependencies.
[04:45] Jill: There are several supply-chain questions - do you perform vendor risk on your critical dependencies, and is open-source usage tracked?
[04:54] Alex: We perform third-party risk assessments for critical infra and security tooling. We maintain an SBOM-like inventory for runtime dependencies and can provide high-level statements about patch cadence and CVE remediation. Not every low-level OSS component will be enumerated in the SIG, but we can provide guidance and escalate if your team needs deeper detail.
[05:15] Tom: Our vendor security team sometimes asks for encryption key rotation cadence and the ability to revoke keys quickly. Can you revoke keys and what is the RTO for key rotation?
[05:24] Priya: Key rotation depends on the KMS in use. For cloud-managed KMS we have automated rotation policies and can rotate on demand with typical propagation within minutes for new keys, and we support emergency revocation workflows for Private deployments. We'll document example SLAs for key rotation/revocation.
[05:42] Jill: A few items in the SIG are tickboxes - e.g., 'We support cross-region replication' or 'Data is encrypted at rest'. Would you mind if we mark some of these as conditional depending on deployment model?
[05:51] Alex: Absolutely - we'll annotate each checkbox with the scope (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and mark any 'Conditional' answers with guidance.
[06:05] Maria: Regarding legal/contract stuff - does Redwood sign a BAA for PHI?
[06:12] Alex: We do have customers with PHI requirements and can discuss a BAA; procurement should confirm the specific requirements and we'll triage to legal. Tom, maybe you can note that as a procurement follow-up.
[06:21] Tom: Yep will do.
[06:24] Priya: One technical point on audit logs - the SIG asks about integrity and retention. We use append-only write patterns with immutability flags in storage, and logs can be exported to your SIEM daily. We'll include example log schema and retention configuration.
[06:39] Jill: For incident response, do you provide playbooks or support during incidents?
[06:45] Alex: We have an incident response process and customer-facing incident notification channels; for enterprise customers we offer incident war rooms and a designated security contact. We'll include the incident response overview and typical notification SLAs.
[06:58] Maria: On ISO, do you have an ISO 27001 certification?
[07:03] Priya: We don't currently have ISO 27001 certification - it's on the roadmap. We'll be explicit in the SIG answer and provide compensating controls and our current security program details.
[07:13] Jill: The questionnaire is also asking for the location of backups and whether backups are encrypted.
[07:18] Priya: Backups are encrypted at rest with AES-256 and stored in region; for cross-region backups we'll call out the specific regions for your configuration. For Dedicated/Private, backup location is under customer control.
[07:30] Alex: Another common evidence request is 'a sample of audit logs' - for privacy we usually provide schema and a synthetic/sample log with similar fields. If they insist on raw logs, we handle it under NDA and with redaction.
[07:44] Tom: That should be fine, our team mostly wants to validate the log fields.
[07:49] Jill: The SIG has a question about change management - do you have documented change control and release management?
[07:56] Priya: Yes, change management is tracked in our internal systems; we have release cadences, rollbacks, and can provide a high-level change control description and timeframe of deployment windows.
[08:08] Alex: For the SIG 'evidence' column where they're asking for file names, we'll upload a ZIP to a secure share with links and list what each file is - SOC2.pdf, PenTest-summary.pdf, Infra-diagram-redacted.pdf, Audit-log-sample.json, etc.
[08:22] Maria: Will that be OK for our vendor risk portal? They usually want links that can be consumed directly.
[08:28] Alex: Yes we'll provide pre-signed links and can set expirations or access restrictions.
[08:33] Jill: A couple of small gotchas: the SIG's 'Data destruction' question - they want to know how you handle customer deletions and end-of-contract data purging.
[08:42] Priya: We have a documented data deletion workflow; for hosted customers we purge tenant data within X days of contract termination or on request, and we'll provide the exact deletion flows and confirmation artifacts. For Dedicated/Private it's typically under customer control but we can support verification. We'll include the SLA numbers.
[08:58] Tom: Anything we should be aware of around model artifacts - like the model weights or logs that might contain PII?
[09:06] Priya: Good question. By default, models are stateless with respect to training; we do not use customer data to train shared models. For logs containing customer PII we'd redact or follow your data handling rules; we'll put conservative language in the SIG and call out options for stricter redaction or on-prem inference.
[09:26] Jill: The vendor form also asks if you have a dedicated security contact.
[09:30] Alex: Yes - we have a security team contact (security@redwood.com) and an assigned security liaison for enterprise deals; we'll provide the contact and escalation path.
[09:39] Maria: Are there any known issues or open items we should be aware of?
[09:43] Priya: Nothing material to call out; we'll include maturity notes like ISO not yet certified and some third-party dependencies. We'll be explicit about what is in scope.
[09:55] Alex: Ok let's go piece-by-piece through the SIG - I'll read the first section and Priya will chime in on technical bits.
[10:04] [walkthrough continues with Alex reading the SIG entries and Priya clarifying]
[20:12] Priya: On questions about data encryption keys - the SIG asks if keys are exportable. For hosted, keys are not exportable from the cloud provider HSM. For Private we can support customer HSMs where the customer controls export policies.
[20:28] Jill: For the auditing section, your answer says logs are immutable - can we get more detail on how immutability is enforced?
[20:33] Priya: We use storage-level immutability features and maintain checksums; write-once buckets for audit logs with retention and tamper-evidence. We'll provide a short technical note in the evidence packet.
[20:46] Tom: The SIG wants to know about internal pen testing cadence and whether you do continuous scanning.
[20:52] Priya: We do quarterly vulnerability scans and annual external pen tests; critical issues are triaged immediately. We'll include dates of the last pen test and remediation status.
[21:05] Jill: Also, the team would like confirmation that Redwood won't use customer data to improve models without explicit permission.
[21:13] Alex: Correct - we will not use customer-provided content for model training without customer consent. We'll include this in writing and in the contract appendix.
[21:22] Maria: Will you note in the SIG whether logging can be forwarded to our SIEM and if so, how frequently?
[21:27] Priya: Yes - we support log forward to SIEM and S3 buckets; frequency and formats are configurable. We'll include sample config options.
[21:36] Jill: A couple of items in the questionnaire reference 'environment hardening' and CIS benchmarks - do you have compliance with any baseline benchmarks?
[21:44] Priya: We follow industry best practices and can provide a mapping to CIS controls for core hosts; we'll include a control mapping doc.
[21:55] Alex: Alright I think we have the main list of evidence to provide. To recap: SOC2 summary + access process, pen test summary, infra diagram, sample audit logs, redacted change management docs, KMS architecture and rotation policy, and the completed SIG spreadsheet with conditional flags.
[22:12] Jill: That sounds right. We'll compile our top evidence requests and share them with you tomorrow.
[22:18] Tom: On contracting, any minimum term requirements we should factor if we move to Dedicated?
[22:24] Alex: Dedicated typically has reserved commitments (monthly or annual) depending on scale, but we can discuss flexibility during commercial. We'll flag procurement with an initial proposal after the security review.
[22:36] Maria: One last question - does Redwood have a policy for data subject access requests or handling GDPR requests?
[22:43] Priya: We have a DSR process; we can assist customers with their DSR obligations and provide guidance. We'll include the DSR handling steps in the evidence.
[22:52] Jill: Great.
[22:55] Alex: Ok we'll assemble the evidence bundle and get the SIG answers to you by next Friday. Priya do you want to summarize what you'll upload?
[23:04] Priya: Sure - SOC2 summary and how to request the full report, pen test summary, infra diagram (redacted), sample audit logs, KMS/key rotation documentation, RBAC and SSO config notes, and a completed SIG spreadsheet with notes for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[23:21] Jill: Perfect. We'll also send a prioritized list of the top 10 evidence items.
[23:27] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and propose times for a follow-up the week of August 25th to walk through any remaining items.
[23:37] Maria: Thanks folks.
[23:39] Tom: Thanks, bye.
[23:41] [call ends]

Notes: Transcript contains typical transcription artifacts; product names occasionally shortened (e.g., K V cache, Redwood Dedicated typed as "Dedciated" in parts). Evidence links to be provided via secure share (pre-signed S3 links) and through the vendor portal.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim from call):
- Redwood to upload completed SIG spreadsheet with annotations for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Redwood to provide SOC2 Type II summary and pen test exec summary.
- Redwood to provide redacted infra diagram and sample audit logs.
- Montclair to send prioritized evidence list and confirm whether a BAA is required.

End of transcript.
